s: pre-Kantian, coming before Immanuel Kant, the philosopher
to appear, to occur (in a given location or situation)
Irene Adler ist eine der bemerkenswertesten Figuren in der Sherlock-Holmes-Serie, obwohl sie nur in einer einzigen Geschichte vorkommt.
Irene Adler is one of the most notable characters in the Sherlock Holmes series, despite appearing in only one story.
to occur, to happen (with some regularity)
Keine Sorge, sowas kommt ganz selten vor.
Don't worry, this kind of thing happens very rarely.
Solche Fälle sollen auch schon vorgekommen sein.
Such cases are purported to have happened already, as well.
to seem, to appear: to feel (oneself to be smart, stupid, clever, dumb, etc., at a specific point in time)
Ich komme mir wie ein Idiot vor.
vorkommen.et: From Middle High German vorekomen, forekomen, vurekomen, vürekomen, from Old High German furaqueman, furakweman, furiqueman, furikweman, from Proto-West Germanic *forakweman, from Proto-Germanic *furaikwemaną, equivalent to vor- + kommen. Cognate with English …

s: taster (of food before it is served, especially an agent employed to prevent poisonings)
to take to task, to give (someone) a good talking-to
to put on display, show off
incident (anything noteworthy happening that goes beyond pure routine)
without any incident, with nothing to report
recently, a short time ago, not long ago, a short while ago, a little while ago
in front of the person implied; straight ahead
